meta.title: Solti — Controlled task execution for Rust systems
meta.description: Open-source control layers for application-owned task execution. Supervise Tokio work, build task-execution agents, or coordinate desired work across agents.

hero.title: Compose systems.
hero.lede: Control what runs, what replaces it, and what happens next.

problem.title: Execution needs an owner.
problem.lede: A task starts as code. Then retries, cancellation, replacement, status, output, shutdown, and rollout state accumulate around it. Without an explicit boundary, control logic scatters across the application.

items.title: New work collides with work already running.
items.body: The system must decide what waits, what is replaced, and when cleanup is complete.

items.title: Each operation grows another control endpoint.
items.body: Submission, status, output, cancellation, and shutdown need one consistent contract.

items.title: Desired changes become endpoint-by-endpoint work.
items.body: Target selection, install, update, removal, and per-agent rollout state need coordination.

idea.title: Declare the work. Keep control of execution.
idea.lede: Solti separates desired work, controlled execution, and runtime evidence. Your application keeps the workload; each product owns one control boundary around it.

steps.title: Desired work
steps.body: Express intent as an application-owned unit of work or a versioned Task.

steps.title: Controlled execution
steps.body: Apply lifecycle, routing, or rollout policy at the boundary that needs it.

steps.title: Runtime evidence
steps.body: Return final outcomes and observed state to the code or system that declared the work.

idea.principle: Choose the boundary the system actually needs. Do not adopt the rest by default.

components.title: One idea. Three explicit boundaries.
components.lede: Taskvisor owns the in-process lifecycle. SDK builds an agent boundary. Podium coordinates compatible agent endpoints. Each can be adopted at its own boundary.

levels.title: Own the lifecycle around Tokio work.
levels.body: Turn async work into a managed lifecycle with retry policy, attempt timeouts, cooperative cancellation, joined shutdown, and direct final outcomes for watched work. Optionally queue, replace, or reject competing work by application key.

levels.title: Turn a Rust binary into a task-execution agent.
levels.body: Accept versioned Tasks, reconcile the latest intent, route each workload to subprocess, native containerd 2.x on Linux, or an application-owned runner, and expose observed state through HTTP or gRPC.

levels.title: Stop operating agents one at a time.
levels.body: Define a task once. Podium reconciles installs, updates, and removals across selected compatible agents, with rollout state for every target. Agents remain responsible for execution.

useCases.title: See each boundary in real work.
useCases.lede: Each component addresses a different control boundary. Start with the one that matches the problem you have now.

items.title: New work arrives before cleanup finishes.
items.body: Run different tenant syncs independently. For the same tenant, cancel the active revision, replace the waiting candidate when a newer revision arrives, and start only after cleanup.

items.title: A daemon needs one Task API.
items.body: Accept versioned subprocess Tasks through HTTP instead of inventing a new endpoint for every operation. Keep supervision, Task state, and shutdown behind the same agent boundary.

items.title: One desired task must reach several agents.
items.body: Select compatible agents once. Reconcile install, update, or removal per target, and inspect rollout state instead of driving every endpoint by hand.

proof.title: Desired work in. Runtime evidence out.
proof.lede: The SDK subprocess example is deliberately ordinary. That is the point: define what should run once, then let the agent own routing, supervision, status, output, and shutdown.
proof.note: Core state and live output are process-local.

fit.title: You may need something smaller.
fit.lede: Solti is useful when execution itself needs policy, observed state, or an API another system can drive. It is not the answer to every background task.

choices.need: One retried future or a fixed worker set
choices.answer: Tokio primitives and a focused retry helper may be enough.

choices.need: Work that must survive process restarts
Application-owned execution with explicit control boundaries

commons.title: See the runtime as a system.
commons.body: Agent Overview is an Apache-2.0 Grafana dashboard for fleet health, task state, lifecycle, API, discovery, and host metrics in one operational view.

openSource.title: Use one component. Shape the next boundary.
openSource.body: Start with a runnable example. Open an issue when a contract does not fit. Contribute a focused fix, example, runner, dashboard, or document when you know what should change.
